newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Thai Farmers Bank B/C individual.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Thai Farmers Bank B/C individual.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Monday it had assigned an individual rating of B/C and and a legal rating of 2 to Thai Farmers Bank, Thailand's third largest commercial bank.

IBCA said in a statement, the rating reflects the prospective deterioration in Thailand's economic environment, which could be expected to some degree to negatively impact Thai Farmers Bank's balance sheet.
"The bank's good performance record would warrant a higher ranking, was it not for the uncertainty created by Thailand's impending economic slowdown," IBCA said.
It said Thai Farmers Bank had developed a reputation for being a modern and progressive bank.

"In 1993 it commenced an extensive re-engineering programme, designed to ensure the bank was well placed to respond to increased competition in the Thai banking sector, that has entailed improvement in service delivery channels and development of its capital markets capabilities," IBCA said.

"As with other Thai banks, it has benefited from a favourable operating environment in recent years, although the country's impending economic slowdown is expected to have some impact on the quality of the bank's loan book."
"Notwithstanding, Thai Farmers Bank has provided more than it has needed to in years of good profitability in order to reduce the impact of future loan losses," IBCA said.

It said the individual rating is an evaluation of a bank's financial strength based on the premise that the bank is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners. The highest Individual rating awarded by IBCA is A.
Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if it ran into difficulties, IBCA said.
